text:
anya: quick heads-up - we need to pick the canonical SDK listing model (iterator vs pages) and how retries/prefetch/resume tokens behave across py/ts/go. constraints: simple defaults for app devs, clear escape hatches for infra, small tokens for mobile.
sam: lean toward iterator as default in py/ts + Stream in go. offer `.byPage()` for power users. keeps main path ergonomic.
noah: important: define where the commit point is. if iterator auto-retries pages we risk duplicates. propose iterator exposes `resume_token` and an optional `ack()` call. default semantics = at-least-once; provide strict/at-most-once if server supports checkpoints.
maya: default transport = unary paged RPC (easier retries per page). streaming pages opt-in for low-latency big lists. streaming reconnects should resume from last saved token but document potential replay of the last N items.
anya: token size limit thoughts? previously 1KB was floated, but for mobile let's cap at 512 bytes. opaque, base64, HMAC-able.
sam: SDK knobs: `retry_policy` (default exp backoff), `prefetch` (default 1), `strict_retry` toggle, `token_size_limit`. `prefetch=1` keeps latency predictable. platform can tune higher.
noah: telemetry request: emit retry_count, reconnect_count, resume_token_len, prefetch_used. Console should let ops filter by region/fallback.
maya: security: resume tokens should be HMAC'd per-tenant and optionally time-limited for Private deployments. add flag for non-replayable session tokens.
infra-bot: compat-check queued: 0 failures. will run on RFC PR.
anya: actions: sam -> draft SDK examples + `byPage()` sketch (due Wed). noah -> write idempotency checklist for runtime (due Mon). maya -> token format + security note (due Tue). infra-bot -> run compat on RFC submit.
sam: question - expose raw page fetch API? i think yes but mark experimental (e.g., `client._fetch_page()` or `client.pages()`).
anya: agree. one more: should we support a debug "no-retries" mode? useful for integrations doing their own dedupe.
noah: add `retry_policy=Retry.none()` or `strict()` and `prefetch=0`. that should cover debug use-cases.
anya: cool. i'll stitch up a short RFC (iterator + stream + token spec) and ping this channel. please add inline comments when i post the PR. thanks :rocket:
